Varda described it as a gift made for him before the end: a loving reconstruction of the boy who became the director of The Umbrellas of Cherbourg.

Daoud Abd El Sayed's comedy is one of the most warmly loved Egyptian films of its era — a portrait of a man who experiences life with an intensity and freedom unavailable to those who can see, set among the ramshackle architecture and human texture of an older Cairo that was already disappearing.

Title: Once Upon a Time in China

Tsui Hark's martial arts epic launched one of Hong Kong cinema's great franchises and made Jet Li a star, with its wire-assisted action sequences — particularly the climactic ladder fight — representing a quantum leap in action choreography that influenced the genre for decades.

Title: Only Yesterday

Isao Takahata's Studio Ghibli film, adapted from Hotaru Okamoto and Yuko Tone's manga, is remarkable for the sensitivity and precision with which it reconstructs childhood memory: the particular texture of the past, and the way an adult self is shaped by experiences long believed forgotten.

Title: Riki-Oh: The Story of Ricky

Based on a Japanese manga, Lam Nai-choi's Hong Kong film achieves a cult legendary status through the sheer inventive excess of its practical gore effects, which are so extreme as to function as comedy — a film of absolute sincerity operating well beyond the normal register of exploitation cinema.

Title: Thalapathi

Mani Ratnam's Tamil epic, starring Rajinikanth as Surya and Mammootty as Devaraj, is one of the great films of South Indian cinema — an emotional and action-filled work that takes the genre of the friendship film seriously as tragedy, with Ilayaraaja's score providing much of its emotional weight.

Title: The Five Heartbeats

Robert Townsend's affectionate and encyclopedic film draws on the histories of many real groups — the Temptations, the Dells, the Ink Spots — to construct a panoramic portrait of Black American popular music over three decades, with strong performances from the ensemble cast and a particular sensitivity to the compromises the music industry extracted from its Black artists.

Title: Until the End of the World

Their pursuit across multiple continents (France, Russia, China, Japan, Australia) ultimately leads to an Aboriginal community in the Australian desert, where the device's discovery that dream-images can be recorded becomes an obsession that threatens to consume everyone. Wim Wenders's ambitious, sprawling science-fiction road movie, originally released in a shorter form, exists in a director's cut running nearly five hours; either version is a unique achievement in world cinema.
